newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zedillo says "nothing hurts" a Mexican president.
newsitem.headline: Zedillo says "nothing hurts" a Mexican president.

text.p: President Ernesto Zedillo on Wednesday said "nothing hurts" a Mexican head of state, dismissing claims his image had been dented by a new rebel uprising in the south of the country.
"Fortunately, for a Mexican president, nothing hurts him," Zedillo, who has been branded by many Mexicans as a weak leader, said in the first part of an interview broadcast on Mexico's Canal 40.
He was responding to a question about whether his image has been affected by the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) rebellion launched in June.
The rebels carried out their most bloody strikes just days before Zedillo's Sept. 1 annual State of the Nation address, which many saw as an attempt to upstage him.
"It's a group that comes up, erupts with tremendous violence and has killed several dozen people," he said, adding that the rebellion is nevertheless a worry for him and many Mexicans.
